answer: Each additional ongoing medical condition (MHONGO='Yes') is associated with a +28.76% increase in the odds of higher COVID-19 severity (OR 1.29, 95% CI −2.16% to +69.45%, p=0.071), independent of BCG vaccination status and patient-interaction variables (work hours, patients seen, expected interaction), per a proportional-odds ordinal regression on COVID cases (n=153, ordinal severity 1–4 = maximum AESEV per patient). Caveat: the proportional-odds assumption was violated for this exposure (the effect is driven by the severe/critical grades, so the single OR is a weighted average), and the primary sample is small (p=0.07), although wider-sample sensitivity models were statistically significant and consistent in direction.
